solution:
By parts (LIATE: the logarithm is 'L', so take it as \(u\)): \(u = \log x,\ dv = x^2\, dx\), giving \(du = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\).
Using \(\int u\, dv = uv - \int v\, du\):
\(\int x^2\log x\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \int \dfrac{x^3}{3}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \dfrac{1}{3}\int x^2\, dx\)
\(= \dfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \dfrac{x^3}{9} + c\)

By parts with \(u = x^2\) (the algebraic part) and \(dv = \sin 3x\, dx\), so \(du = 2x\, dx,\ v = -\dfrac{\cos 3x}{3}\):
\(\int x^2\sin 3x\, dx = -\dfrac{x^2\cos 3x}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\int x\cos 3x\, dx\)
For \(\int x\cos 3x\, dx\), again by parts (\(u=x,\ dv=\cos 3x\, dx,\ v=\dfrac{\sin 3x}{3}\)):
\(\int x\cos 3x\, dx = \dfrac{x\sin 3x}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\int \sin 3x\, dx = \dfrac{x\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\cos 3x}{9}\)
Hence \(\int x^2\sin 3x\, dx = -\dfrac{x^2\cos 3x}{3} + \dfrac{2x\sin 3x}{9} + \dfrac{2\cos 3x}{27} + c\)

By parts (LIATE: inverse-trig is 'I', take it as \(u\)): \(u = \tan^{-1} x,\ dv = x\, dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\):
\(\int x\tan^{-1} x\, dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\, dx\)
Since \(\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\), \(\int \dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\, dx = x - \tan^{-1} x\).
\(= \dfrac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \tan^{-1} x\right) = \dfrac{(x^2+1)}{2}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{x}{2} + c\)

By parts with \(u = \tan^{-1} x\) (inverse-trig, 'I') and \(dv = x^2\, dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\):
\(\int x^2\tan^{-1} x\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{x^3}{1+x^2}\, dx\)
Since \(\dfrac{x^3}{1+x^2} = x - \dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\), \(\int \dfrac{x^3}{1+x^2}\, dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2)\).
\(= \dfrac{x^3}{3}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{x^2}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6}\log(1+x^2) + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key's second term is \(-\frac{x}{12}(x^3-3x)\), carrying an extra \(x\) in the coefficient; it should be \(-\frac{1}{12}(x^3-3x)\). The answer below is correct.]

By parts with \(u = \tan^{-1} x\) and \(dv = x^3\, dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\):
\(\int x^3\tan^{-1} x\, dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{4}\int \dfrac{x^4}{1+x^2}\, dx\)
Since \(\dfrac{x^4}{1+x^2} = x^2 - 1 + \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}\), \(\int \dfrac{x^4}{1+x^2}\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - x + \tan^{-1} x\).
\(= \dfrac{x^4}{4}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{x^3}{12} + \dfrac{x}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4}\tan^{-1} x + c\)

Write \((\log x)^2 = (\log x)^2\cdot 1\) and take \(u = (\log x)^2,\ dv = dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{2\log x}{x}\, dx,\ v = x\):
\(\int (\log x)^2\, dx = x(\log x)^2 - \int x\cdot\dfrac{2\log x}{x}\, dx = x(\log x)^2 - 2\int \log x\, dx\)
And \(\int \log x\, dx = x\log x - x\) (by parts). Therefore
\(\int (\log x)^2\, dx = x(\log x)^2 - 2x\log x + 2x + c\)

Write \(\sec^3 x = \sec x\cdot \sec^2 x\) and take \(u = \sec x,\ dv = \sec^2 x\, dx\), so \(du = \sec x\tan x\, dx,\ v = \tan x\). Let \(I = \int \sec^3 x\, dx\):
\(I = \sec x\tan x - \int \tan x\cdot \sec x\tan x\, dx = \sec x\tan x - \int \sec x(\sec^2 x - 1)\, dx\)
\(I = \sec x\tan x - \int \sec^3 x\, dx + \int \sec x\, dx = \sec x\tan x - I + \log|\sec x + \tan x|\)
So \(2I = \sec x\tan x + \log|\sec x + \tan x|\), giving
\(\int \sec^3 x\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\sec x\tan x + \dfrac{1}{2}\log|\sec x + \tan x| + c\)

First reduce the power: \(\sin^2 x = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\), so \(\int x\sin^2 x\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int x\, dx - \dfrac{1}{2}\int x\cos 2x\, dx\).
For \(\int x\cos 2x\, dx\), by parts (\(u = x,\ dv = \cos 2x\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\)):
\(\int x\cos 2x\, dx = \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sin 2x\, dx = \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\)
Hence \(\int x\sin^2 x\, dx = \dfrac{x^2}{4} - \dfrac{x\sin 2x}{4} - \dfrac{\cos 2x}{8} + c\)

By parts (log is 'L'): \(u = \log x,\ dv = x^3\, dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\):
\(\int x^3\log x\, dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \int \dfrac{x^4}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\, dx = \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \dfrac{1}{4}\int x^3\, dx\)
\(= \dfrac{x^4}{4}\log x - \dfrac{x^4}{16} + c\)

Let \(I = \int e^{2x}\cos 3x\, dx\). By parts twice (each time \(u = e^{2x}\)) the integral reproduces itself. Using the standard result \(\int e^{ax}\cos bx\, dx = \dfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2+b^2}(a\cos bx + b\sin bx) + c\) with \(a = 2,\ b = 3\) (so \(a^2+b^2 = 13\)):
\(\int e^{2x}\cos 3x\, dx = \dfrac{e^{2x}}{13}\left(2\cos 3x + 3\sin 3x\right) + c\)

By parts (inverse-trig is 'I'): \(u = \sin^{-1} x,\ dv = x\, dx\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\):
\(\int x\sin^{-1} x\, dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx\)
With \(\dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \dfrac{-(1-x^2)+1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\), one gets \(\int \dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \dfrac{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2}\).
\(= \dfrac{x^2}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^{-1} x + \dfrac{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{4} = \dfrac{(2x^2-1)}{4}\sin^{-1} x + \dfrac{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{4} + c\)

By parts with \(u = \cos^{-1} x\) and \(dv = x^2\, dx\), so \(du = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx,\ v = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\):
\(\int x^2\cos^{-1} x\, dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\cos^{-1} x + \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx\)
Put \(1-x^2 = t\) in the remaining integral: \(\int \dfrac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\, dx = \dfrac{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}{3} - \sqrt{1-x^2}\).
\(= \dfrac{x^3}{3}\cos^{-1} x + \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}{3} - \sqrt{1-x^2}\right] = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\cos^{-1} x - \dfrac{(x^2+2)\sqrt{1-x^2}}{9} + c\)

Put \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\). Then \(\int \dfrac{\log(\log x)}{x}\, dx = \int \log t\, dt\).
By parts, \(\int \log t\, dt = t\log t - t\). Restoring \(t = \log x\):
\(\int \dfrac{\log(\log x)}{x}\, dx = \log x\cdot\log(\log x) - \log x + c\)

By parts with \(u = \sin^{-1} t\) and \(dv = \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\, dt\), so \(du = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\, dt\) and \(v = \int \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\, dt = -\sqrt{1-t^2}\):
\(\int \dfrac{t\sin^{-1} t}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\, dt = -\sqrt{1-t^2}\,\sin^{-1} t + \int \sqrt{1-t^2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}\, dt\)
\(= -\sqrt{1-t^2}\,\sin^{-1} t + \int dt = t - \sqrt{1-t^2}\,\sin^{-1} t + c\)

Put \(t = \sqrt{x}\), so \(x = t^2\) and \(dx = 2t\, dt\): \(\int \cos\sqrt{x}\, dx = 2\int t\cos t\, dt\).
By parts (\(u = t,\ dv = \cos t\, dt,\ v = \sin t\)): \(\int t\cos t\, dt = t\sin t + \cos t\).
\(= 2\left(t\sin t + \cos t\right) = 2\sqrt{x}\,\sin\sqrt{x} + 2\cos\sqrt{x} + c\)

Put \(t = \cos\theta\), so \(dt = -\sin\theta\, d\theta\): \(\int \sin\theta\,\log(\cos\theta)\, d\theta = -\int \log t\, dt\).
Since \(\int \log t\, dt = t\log t - t\) (by parts):
\(= -\left(t\log t - t\right) = -\cos\theta\,\log(\cos\theta) + \cos\theta + c = \cos\theta\left(1 - \log(\cos\theta)\right) + c\)

Reduce the cube: \(\cos^3 x = \dfrac{3\cos x + \cos 3x}{4}\), so \(\int x\cos^3 x\, dx = \dfrac{3}{4}\int x\cos x\, dx + \dfrac{1}{4}\int x\cos 3x\, dx\).
By parts: \(\int x\cos x\, dx = x\sin x + \cos x\) and \(\int x\cos 3x\, dx = \dfrac{x\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\cos 3x}{9}\).
\(= \dfrac{3}{4}\left(x\sin x + \cos x\right) + \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{x\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\cos 3x}{9}\right)\)
\(= \dfrac{3x\sin x}{4} + \dfrac{3\cos x}{4} + \dfrac{x\sin 3x}{12} + \dfrac{\cos 3x}{36} + c\)

Here the integrand is \(\dfrac{\sin\left((\log x)^2\right)}{x}\cdot\log x\). Put \(t = (\log x)^2\), so \(dt = \dfrac{2\log x}{x}\, dx\), i.e. \(\dfrac{\log x}{x}\, dx = \dfrac{dt}{2}\).
\(\int \dfrac{\sin\left((\log x)^2\right)}{x}\cdot\log x\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \sin t\, dt = -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos t\)
\(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos\left((\log x)^2\right) + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(-\frac{1}{2}(\log x)^2\); this differentiates to \(-\frac{\log x}{x}\), the negative of the integrand. The correct answer is \(+\frac{1}{2}(\log x)^2\). The answer below is correct.]

Put \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \dfrac{1}{x}\, dx\). Then \(\int \dfrac{\log x}{x}\, dx = \int t\, dt = \dfrac{t^2}{2}\).
\(= \dfrac{(\log x)^2}{2} + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key is structurally wrong — it prints \(x\sin 3x\) and \(x\sin 7x\) terms (should be \(x\cos 3x\), \(x\cos 7x\)) plus a stray \(\frac{1}{18}\cos x\), and does not differentiate to the integrand. The answer below is correct.]

Convert the product to a sum: \(\sin 2x\cos 5x = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\sin 7x - \sin 3x\right]\), so
\(\int x\sin 2x\cos 5x\, dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int x\sin 7x\, dx - \dfrac{1}{2}\int x\sin 3x\, dx\).
By parts: \(\int x\sin 7x\, dx = -\dfrac{x\cos 7x}{7} + \dfrac{\sin 7x}{49}\) and \(\int x\sin 3x\, dx = -\dfrac{x\cos 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{9}\).
\(= -\dfrac{x\cos 7x}{14} + \dfrac{\sin 7x}{98} + \dfrac{x\cos 3x}{6} - \dfrac{\sin 3x}{18} + c\)

Put \(t = x^{1/3}\), so \(x = t^3\) and \(dx = 3t^2\, dt\): \(\int \cos\left(\sqrt[3]{x}\right)\, dx = 3\int t^2\cos t\, dt\).
By parts twice: \(\int t^2\cos t\, dt = t^2\sin t - 2\int t\sin t\, dt = t^2\sin t + 2t\cos t - 2\sin t\).
\(= 3\left(t^2\sin t + 2t\cos t - 2\sin t\right) = 3x^{2/3}\sin\left(\sqrt[3]{x}\right) + 6\sqrt[3]{x}\,\cos\left(\sqrt[3]{x}\right) - 6\sin\left(\sqrt[3]{x}\right) + c\)

Let \(I = \int e^{2x}\sin 3x\, dx\). This is the recurring type; using \(\int e^{ax}\sin bx\, dx = \dfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2+b^2}(a\sin bx - b\cos bx) + c\) with \(a = 2,\ b = 3\) (so \(a^2+b^2 = 13\)):
\(\int e^{2x}\sin 3x\, dx = \dfrac{e^{2x}}{13}\left(2\sin 3x - 3\cos 3x\right) + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\frac{e^{-x}}{5}[-\cos x + 2\sin 2x]\) with the argument \(\cos x\) instead of \(\cos 2x\); the correct answer is \(\frac{e^{-x}}{5}(2\sin 2x - \cos 2x)\). The answer below is correct.]

Let \(I = \int e^{-x}\cos 2x\, dx\). Using \(\int e^{ax}\cos bx\, dx = \dfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2+b^2}(a\cos bx + b\sin bx) + c\) with \(a = -1,\ b = 2\) (so \(a^2+b^2 = 5\)):
\(\int e^{-x}\cos 2x\, dx = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{5}\left(-\cos 2x + 2\sin 2x\right) = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{5}\left(2\sin 2x - \cos 2x\right) + c\)

Let \(I = \int \sin(\log x)\, dx\). By parts (\(u = \sin(\log x),\ dv = dx,\ v = x\)):
\(I = x\sin(\log x) - \int \cos(\log x)\, dx\).
For \(J = \int \cos(\log x)\, dx\), again by parts: \(J = x\cos(\log x) + \int \sin(\log x)\, dx = x\cos(\log x) + I\).
Substituting: \(I = x\sin(\log x) - x\cos(\log x) - I\), so \(2I = x\left[\sin(\log x) - \cos(\log x)\right]\).
\(\int \sin(\log x)\, dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\left[\sin(\log x) - \cos(\log x)\right] + c\)

Write \(\sqrt{5x^2+3} = \sqrt{5}\,\sqrt{x^2 + \tfrac{3}{5}}\). Using \(\int \sqrt{x^2+a^2}\, dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2+a^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2+a^2}\right|\) with \(a^2 = \tfrac{3}{5}\):
\(\int \sqrt{5x^2+3}\, dx = \sqrt{5}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{5}} + \dfrac{3}{10}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{5}}\right|\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{5x^2+3} + \dfrac{3\sqrt{5}}{10}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{5}}\right| + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives the second coefficient as \(\frac{a^2}{2}\); the substitution \(t=x^3\) puts a factor \(\frac{1}{3}\) on both terms, so it should be \(\frac{a^2}{6}\). The answer below is correct.]

Put \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\, dx\), i.e. \(x^2\, dx = \dfrac{dt}{3}\): \(\int x^2\sqrt{a^2 - x^6}\, dx = \dfrac{1}{3}\int \sqrt{a^2 - t^2}\, dt\).
Using \(\int \sqrt{a^2-t^2}\, dt = \dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{a^2-t^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{t}{a}\):
\(= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{a^2-t^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{t}{a}\right] = \dfrac{x^3}{6}\sqrt{a^2 - x^6} + \dfrac{a^2}{6}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x^3}{a} + c\)

Expand and complete the square: \((x-3)(7-x) = -x^2 + 10x - 21 = 4 - (x-5)^2\).
Using \(\int \sqrt{a^2-u^2}\, du = \dfrac{u}{2}\sqrt{a^2-u^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{u}{a}\) with \(u = x-5,\ a = 2\):
\(\int \sqrt{(x-3)(7-x)}\, dx = \dfrac{x-5}{2}\sqrt{(x-3)(7-x)} + 2\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-5}{2}\right) + c\)

Note \(\sqrt{4^x(4^x+4)} = 2^x\sqrt{4^x+4}\). Put \(t = 2^x\), so \(dt = 2^x\log 2\, dx\), i.e. \(dx = \dfrac{dt}{t\log 2}\), and \(4^x = t^2\):
\(\int 2^x\sqrt{4^x+4}\, dx = \int t\sqrt{t^2+4}\cdot\dfrac{dt}{t\log 2} = \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\int \sqrt{t^2+4}\, dt\).
Using \(\int \sqrt{t^2+a^2}\, dt = \dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{t^2+a^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+a^2}\right|\) with \(a = 2\):
\(= \dfrac{1}{\log 2}\left[\dfrac{2^x}{2}\sqrt{4^x+4} + 2\log\left(2^x + \sqrt{4^x+4}\right)\right] + c\)

Split: \(\int (x+1)\sqrt{2x^2+3}\, dx = \int x\sqrt{2x^2+3}\, dx + \int \sqrt{2x^2+3}\, dx\).
For the first, put \(w = 2x^2+3\ (dw = 4x\, dx)\): \(\int x\sqrt{2x^2+3}\, dx = \dfrac{1}{4}\int \sqrt{w}\, dw = \dfrac{(2x^2+3)^{3/2}}{6}\).
For the second, \(\sqrt{2x^2+3} = \sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{2}}\), so \(\int \sqrt{2x^2+3}\, dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{2x^2+3} + \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{2}}\right|\).
\(= \dfrac{(2x^2+3)^{3/2}}{6} + \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{2x^2+3} + \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\log\left|x + \sqrt{x^2+\tfrac{3}{2}}\right| + c\)

Put \(t = \tan x\), so \(dt = \sec^2 x\, dx\): \(\int \sec^2 x\,\sqrt{\tan^2 x + \tan x - 7}\, dx = \int \sqrt{t^2 + t - 7}\, dt\).
Complete the square: \(t^2 + t - 7 = \left(t + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \tfrac{29}{4}\). Using \(\int \sqrt{u^2-a^2}\, du = \dfrac{u}{2}\sqrt{u^2-a^2} - \dfrac{a^2}{2}\log\left|u + \sqrt{u^2-a^2}\right|\) with \(u = t+\tfrac{1}{2},\ a^2 = \tfrac{29}{4}\):
\(= \dfrac{2\tan x + 1}{4}\sqrt{\tan^2 x + \tan x - 7} - \dfrac{29}{8}\log\left|\tan x + \tfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{\tan^2 x + \tan x - 7}\right| + c\)

Complete the square: \(x^2 + 2x + 5 = (x+1)^2 + 4\). Using \(\int \sqrt{u^2+a^2}\, du = \dfrac{u}{2}\sqrt{u^2+a^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\log\left|u + \sqrt{u^2+a^2}\right|\) with \(u = x+1,\ a = 2\):
\(\int \sqrt{x^2+2x+5}\, dx = \dfrac{x+1}{2}\sqrt{x^2+2x+5} + 2\log\left|x+1 + \sqrt{x^2+2x+5}\right| + c\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key's log coefficient evaluates to \(\frac{23}{16}\); the correct coefficient is \(\sqrt{2}\cdot\frac{a^2}{2} = \frac{23\sqrt{2}}{32}\) (with \(a^2=\frac{23}{16}\)). The answer below is correct.]

Take out \(\sqrt{2}\) and complete the square: \(2x^2+3x+4 = 2\left[\left(x+\tfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 + \tfrac{23}{16}\right]\), so \(\sqrt{2x^2+3x+4} = \sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{\left(x+\tfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 + \tfrac{23}{16}}\).
Using \(\int \sqrt{u^2+a^2}\, du = \dfrac{u}{2}\sqrt{u^2+a^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\log\left|u + \sqrt{u^2+a^2}\right|\) with \(u = x+\tfrac{3}{4},\ a^2 = \tfrac{23}{16}\):
\(\int \sqrt{2x^2+3x+4}\, dx = \dfrac{4x+3}{8}\sqrt{2x^2+3x+4} + \dfrac{23\sqrt{2}}{32}\log\left|x + \tfrac{3}{4} + \sqrt{x^2 + \tfrac{3}{2}x + 2}\right| + c\)

Use the rule \(\int e^x\left[f(x) + f'(x)\right]\, dx = e^x f(x) + c\). Take \(f(x) = 2 + \cot x\), so \(f'(x) = -\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\), and indeed \(f(x) + f'(x) = 2 + \cot x - \operatorname{cosec}^2 x\).
\(\int (2 + \cot x - \operatorname{cosec}^2 x)e^x\, dx = e^x(2 + \cot x) + c\)

Simplify using half-angles: \(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\tfrac{x}{2}\) and \(1 + \sin x = 1 + 2\sin\tfrac{x}{2}\cos\tfrac{x}{2}\), so
\(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x} = \tan\tfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2}\).
This has the form \(f(x) + f'(x)\) with \(f(x) = \tan\tfrac{x}{2}\) (since \(f'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2}\)). Hence by \(\int e^x[f+f']\, dx = e^x f\):
\(\int \left(\dfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\right)e^x\, dx = e^x\tan\tfrac{x}{2} + c\)

This has the form \(\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\, dx = e^x f(x) + c\). Take \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), so \(f'(x) = -\dfrac{1}{x^2}\), and \(f(x)+f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x^2}\).
\(\int e^x\left(\dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)\, dx = \dfrac{e^x}{x} + c\)

Rewrite \(\dfrac{x}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{(x+1)-1}{(x+1)^2} = \dfrac{1}{x+1} - \dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}\). This is \(f(x)+f'(x)\) with \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x+1}\) (so \(f'(x) = -\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}\)).
By \(\int e^x[f+f']\, dx = e^x f\):
\(\int \left(\dfrac{x}{(x+1)^2}\right)e^x\, dx = \dfrac{e^x}{x+1} + c\)

Distribute: \(\dfrac{e^x}{x}\left[x(\log x)^2 + 2\log x\right] = e^x\left[(\log x)^2 + \dfrac{2\log x}{x}\right]\).
This is \(f(x)+f'(x)\) with \(f(x) = (\log x)^2\) (so \(f'(x) = \dfrac{2\log x}{x}\)). By \(\int e^x[f+f']\, dx = e^x f\):
\(\int \dfrac{e^x}{x}\left[x(\log x)^2 + 2\log x\right]\, dx = e^x(\log x)^2 + c\)

Distribute: \(e^{5x}\left(\dfrac{5x\log x + 1}{x}\right) = e^{5x}\left[5\log x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right]\).
This matches \(\int e^{ax}\left[a f(x) + f'(x)\right]\, dx = e^{ax} f(x) + c\) with \(a = 5\) and \(f(x) = \log x\) (so \(a f = 5\log x,\ f' = \tfrac{1}{x}\)).
\(\int e^{5x}\left(\dfrac{5x\log x + 1}{x}\right)\, dx = e^{5x}\log x + c\)

Split off \(e^{\sin^{-1} x}\): the integrand is \(e^{\sin^{-1} x}\left[\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} + 1\right]\). Put \(t = \sin^{-1} x\), so \(x = \sin t,\ \sqrt{1-x^2} = \cos t,\ dx = \cos t\, dt\):
\(\int e^{t}\left(\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t} + 1\right)\cos t\, dt = \int e^{t}(\sin t + \cos t)\, dt\).
Since \(\int e^{t}[f(t)+f'(t)]\, dt = e^{t}f(t)\) with \(f(t) = \sin t\) (\(f'(t) = \cos t\)): \(= e^{t}\sin t\).
Restoring \(t = \sin^{-1} x\) (so \(\sin t = x\)): \(\int e^{\sin^{-1} x}\left(\dfrac{x + \sqrt{1-x^2}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)\, dx = x\,e^{\sin^{-1} x} + c\)

By the logarithm law \(\log(1+x)^{(1+x)} = (1+x)\log(1+x)\). Put \(u = 1+x\ (du = dx)\): \(\int (1+x)\log(1+x)\, dx = \int u\log u\, du\).
By parts (\(u\)-part \(= \log u,\ dv = u\, du,\ v = \tfrac{u^2}{2}\)): \(\int u\log u\, du = \dfrac{u^2}{2}\log u - \int \dfrac{u^2}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{u}\, du = \dfrac{u^2}{2}\log u - \dfrac{u^2}{4}\).
\(\int \log(1+x)^{(1+x)}\, dx = \dfrac{(1+x)^2}{2}\log(1+x) - \dfrac{(1+x)^2}{4} + c\)

Put \(t = \log x\), so \(x = e^{t}\) and \(dx = e^{t}\, dt\):
\(\int \operatorname{cosec}(\log x)\left[1 - \cot(\log x)\right]\, dx = \int e^{t}\operatorname{cosec} t\left(1 - \cot t\right)\, dt = \int e^{t}\left[\operatorname{cosec} t - \operatorname{cosec} t\cot t\right]\, dt\).
This is \(\int e^{t}[f(t)+f'(t)]\, dt = e^{t}f(t)\) with \(f(t) = \operatorname{cosec} t\) (since \(f'(t) = -\operatorname{cosec} t\cot t\)). So \(= e^{t}\operatorname{cosec} t\).
Restoring \(t = \log x\): \(\int \operatorname{cosec}(\log x)\left[1 - \cot(\log x)\right]\, dx = x\,\operatorname{cosec}(\log x) + c\)
